headline: A UCL and Moorfields-led project to build a worldwide eye-scan AI model now has 108 partners in more than 40 countries.
score_reason: Progress update on a research project; numbers are the team's own and the model is still being validated.
importance_line: Patients in regions usually missing from medical AI training data could be better served by eye-disease models that include them, and researchers get an open-access model to build on, but validation is still months away and the talk's date is not given.
summary: Ophthalmology Times reports that Paul Nderitu of UCL and Moorfields Eye Hospital told the EURETINA 2026 congress in Vienna that Global RETFound, a foundation model (a large general-purpose AI trained on huge amounts of data for many later tasks) for retinal images, has grown to 108 partners from more than 40 countries, with most sharing locally trained image generators and 27 sites sharing real data. The team plans to synthesise about 100 million back-of-eye images, is validating the model at more than 20 sites for conditions from diabetic retinopathy to retinopathy of prematurity, and aims to release it open access for research after validation over the coming months.
notes: Congress date not stated in the text; the talk may predate 3 Oct 2026. Figures are the project's own.
